title: Stop the systemd unit reporting every
notes: - Symptom seen on the production host: each restart logged
`vexa.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=143/n/a` followed by
`Failed with result 'exit-code'`, so the unit sat in a failed state after a
finishes its cleanup and then calls `process.exit(143)` for `SIGTERM` on
purpose, "so that Node.js treats this as a signal termination, not a normal
exit code as success. Adding an app-level signal handler would have been the
wrong fix: it would race Next's own graceful shutdown.
result: `SuccessExitStatus=143` added to `deploy/vexa.service` and to the live unit on the production host.
evidence: after `daemon-reload` and `systemctl restart vexa`, the journal shows only `Stopped` / `Started` with no `Failed` line, and `systemctl show` reports `Result=success`, `ActiveState=active`. Health endpoint, loopback-only bind and public `/login` (200) all re-checked.
files: plus `/etc/systemd/system/vexa.service` on the production host (backed up alongside as `.bak-20260827`)
